facts.statement: Natovenator was a dromaeosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Natovenator is a genus of halszkaraptorine dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Natovenator lived approximately 72 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadaemnte 72 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPC-D 102/114 was discovered in the Barun Goyot Formation of Omnogovi Province, Mongolia.
facts.quote: The Natovenator holotype specimen, MPC-D 102/114, was found in sediments of the Barun Goyot Formation of Omnogovi Province, Mongolia.

facts.statement: Natovenator polydontus was formally described in 2022 by a team including Sungjin Lee, Yuong-Nam Lee, and Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: In 2022, Natovenator polydontus was described as a new genus and species of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaurs by Sungjin Lee, Yuong-Nam Lee, Philip J. Currie, Robin Sissons, Jin-Young Park, Su-Hwan Kim, Rinchen Barsbold, and Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar based on these remains.

facts.statement: The genus name Natovenator means "swimming hunter" in Latin, referencing its likely piscivorous diet and swimming behavior.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Natovenator", is derived from the Latin words "nato", meaning "to swim", and "venator", meaning "hunter", in reference to its piscivorous diet and possible swimming behaviour.

facts.statement: The specific name polydontus means "many-toothed" in Greek.
facts.quote: The specific name, "polydontus", is derived from the Greek words "polys", meaning "many", and "odous", meaning "tooth".

facts.statement: Natovenator was a very small theropod that resembled extant waterfowl in appearance.
facts.quote: Natovenator was a very small theropod, comparable in appearance to extant waterfowl, like other members of the Halszkaraptorinae.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Natovenator's length at 0.7 meters and weight at 0.3 kilograms.
facts.quote: In the third edition of The Princeton Field Guide to Dinosaurs, Gregory S. Paul stated its length at 0.7 m and weight at 0.3 kg.

facts.statement: Natovenator possessed unique features including 13 large, incisiviform premaxillary teeth, an hourglass-shaped metacarpal II, and an elongated internarial process on the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Natovenator is different from other halszkaraptorines due to features such as a wide groove delimited by a pair of ridges on the anterodorsal surface of the premaxilla, a premaxilla with an elongated internarial process that overlies nasal and extends posterior to the external naris, 13 premaxillary teeth with large and incisiviform crowns, the absence of pleurocoels in cervical vertebrae, and an hourglass-shaped metacarpal II, among other features.

facts.statement: The parapophyses in Natovenator's vertebrae are similar to those of extinct toothed diving birds, the Hesperornithiformes.
facts.quote: The parapophyses in its vertebrae are similar to the extinct Hesperornithiformes, which were toothed diving birds.

facts.statement: Researchers regard Natovenator as an efficient swimmer with a semiaquatic lifestyle.
facts.quote: In 2022, Lee and colleagues regarded Natovenator as an efficient swimming dromaeosaurid with a semiaquatic lifestyle.

facts.statement: Natovenator had a streamlined dorsal rib cage with posteriorly-oriented ribs, a feature also found in efficient diving birds and mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Most notably, its dorsal rib cage had posteriorly-oriented ribs, providing a streamlined shape that is also known in efficient diving birds, mosasaurs, choristoderes, and spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Although its exact swimming mechanics are unknown, researchers suggest Natovenator used its forelimbs as flippers for propulsion.
facts.quote: Even though the exact aquatic locomotion of Natovenator is unknown, Lee and colleagues suggested that its forelimbs acted as flippers for propulsion when swimming.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Natovenator as a derived member of the subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Lee et al. (2022) recovered Natovenator as a derived member of the Halszkaraptorinae, with Halszkaraptor being the most basal member of the group.

facts.statement: Natovenator is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Natovenator belongs to the subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Halszkaraptorinae

facts.statement: Natovenator is crucial for understanding halszkaraptorines because it provides significant support for the proposed semiaquatic lifestyle of this group.
facts.quote: Natovenator is crucial to the understanding of halszkaraptorines due to it providing more support for the semi-aquatic lifestyle that has been proposed for this clade.

facts.statement: Natovenator had a long neck similar to modern diving birds, likely useful for catching prey.
facts.quote: Similar to many modern-day diving birds, the neck of Natovenator was rather long, likely useful in catching/snatching prey.

facts.statement: Fossils of Natovenator come from the Upper Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Sus restos son provenientes de la Formación Barun Goyot del Cretácico Superior en Mongolia.

facts.statement: Researchers in 2022 considered Natovenator an efficient swimming dromaeosaurid with a semi-aquatic lifestyle.
facts.quote: En 2022, Lee y sus colegas consideraron a Natovenator como un dromeosáurido nadador eficiente con un estilo de vida semiacuático.

facts.statement: The team suggested the delayed premaxillary dentition pattern might have allowed Natovenator to continue providing enlarged teeth, similar to sauropterygians.
facts.quote: El equipo indicó que el patrón retrasado de la dentición premaxilar podría haber permitido que siguiera proporcionando dientes agrandados en Natovenator, de manera similar a los sauropterigios.

facts.statement: Like many modern diving birds, Natovenator had a fairly long neck, likely useful for catching prey.
facts.quote: Al igual que muchas aves buceadoras de hoy en día, el cuello de Natovenator era bastante largo, probablemente útil para atraparla presa.

facts.statement: Its dorsal rib cage had backward-oriented ribs providing a hydrodynamic shape also known in efficient diving birds, mosasaurs, choristoderes, and spinosaurs.
facts.quote: En particular, su caja torácica dorsal tenía costillas orientadas hacia atrás, proporcionando una forma hidrodinámica que también se conoce en aves buceadoras eficientes, mosasaurios, coristoderes y espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: Although the exact aquatic locomotion of Natovenator is unknown, researchers suggested its forelimbs acted as flippers to propel itself while swimming.
facts.quote: Aunque se desconoce la locomoción acuática exacta de Natovenator, Lee y sus colegas sugirieron que sus extremidades anteriores actuaban como aletas para propulsarse al nadar.

facts.statement: The Barun Goyot Formation was a desert environment similar to the current area, though Mongolia was known to be slightly wetter during the Mesozoic.
facts.quote: La Formación Barun Goyot era un ambiente desértico, similar al área actual, aunque se sabe que Mongolia fue un poco más húmeda durante el Mesozoico.

facts.statement: The Barun Goyot Formation dates to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: La Formación Barun Goyot data de la etapa Maastrichtiense del Cretácico Superior, hace unos 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: Natovenator belongs to the parent group Halszkaraptorinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Halszkaraptorinae

facts.statement: Natovenator is classified in the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: The time range for Natovenator is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Natovenator.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.quote: The multiple convergences with other aquatic vertebrates include an elongated snout with numerous teeth, delayed replacement pattern of premaxillary teeth, a complex neurovascular system on the snout tip, elongated neck and vertebral zygapophyses, and a retracted, long naris (nostril opening).
